summary: Iteration 3 improved judge score reliability to 80% at 100 (mean 99.0) from iter-2's 70% at 100 (mean 98.5) by switching to an amortized chrono::steady_clock wall-time guard with fast I/O. The prediction of 'reliable 100' was not fully met — 20% of runs still score 95 due to irreducible Docker container timing variance.
key_points: Score: 8/10 runs at 100, 2/10 at 95, mean = 99.0 (up from iter-2: 7/10 at 100, mean = 98.5). Single best score remains 100.

Three mechanism changes all worked as designed: (1) chrono::steady_clock correctly measures wall time instead of CPU time, (2) amortized checking every 512 B&B nodes eliminates chrono overhead, (3) fread/printf fast I/O preserves <25ms algorithm speed.

The 700ms wall-time threshold leaves 300ms for Docker overhead, but container startup + CPU scheduling occasionally exceeds this budget, causing the residual 5-point drops in ~20% of runs — this appears to be an irreducible environment artifact rather than an algorithmic issue.

The algorithm (branch-and-bound with local search fallback) is effectively optimal for this bounded knapsack problem; further score gains would require addressing Docker timing variance (e.g., lowering the timeout further or making the algorithm faster), with diminishing returns from the current 99.0 mean.
